# AI visibility auditing — reference pages

> Three reference pages on measuring whether AI answer engines cite a brand:
> what an AI visibility audit is, what one should cost, and how to check a
> client's citation footprint by hand. Written for SEO consultants and small
> agencies, not for brands buying an audit.

Every URL below resolves to a page matching its description. This file is kept
accurate or removed — a stale llms.txt is worse than no llms.txt, and this site
is held to the same standard it describes.

## Pages

- [What Is an AI Visibility Audit?](https://fercasanovas.github.io/): What an AI visibility audit measures, what it produces, and what separates it from a single chat session or a ranking promise.
- [What Should an AI Visibility Audit Cost?](https://fercasanovas.github.io/what-an-ai-visibility-audit-costs/): The $1,500–$3,000 band for a single-vertical audit, what moves a quote inside it, and what sits below and above that range.
- [How Do You Check Whether a Client Is Being Cited in AI Search?](https://fercasanovas.github.io/how-to-check-ai-citations/): A manual method for checking citation by hand — signed-out sessions, category questions rather than brand questions, repeat checks, and what to record.

## Note on this file

`llms.txt` is a proposed convention, not a standard. None of the answer engines
these pages discuss has published a commitment to reading it, and it is not an
access-control mechanism. It is published here because it is cheap and carries
no known downside, not because it is expected to change anything.
